reusable_findings: Remote scope and Japan eligibility are separate signals; never infer Japan eligibility from Remote alone.
Revenue probability must penalize identity, interview, ongoing-owner-labor, and financial-account gates even when nominal reward is high.
Algora-style bounty routes require checking active bounty status, attempt/competition density, and payout readiness before implementation.
Marketplace open counts are not enough: canonical issue state and repository activity must be verified before treating a bounty as executable.
Stale or superseded bounty listings can remain visible after canonical closure; freshness must be established from the issue/PR source of truth.
Reward ownership matters: a public fixable issue is not a solver revenue route when the bounty is reserved for the original reporter or another role.
AI-oriented bounties attract dense automated competition; high comment/solver density materially lowers payment probability even when the work is AI-completable.
Canonical repository state must outrank marketplace labels such as Featured, Available, or zero solvers; open issue, no competing implementation, and fresh sponsor intent are required before Claim.
Marketplace zero-solver labels can lag reality: a canonical issue may already be closed or have multiple active claim PRs, so zero-solvers is never sufficient evidence of low competition.
